changed_by.title: fix: act only for an account with write access

adam.assumes: With `persist-credentials: false` and no `GH_TOKEN` in the sessions' step, no file a reviewer's `Read` tool can reach on the runner holds the `review` job's token, which now writes to contents, pull requests and issues.
adam.if_wrong: Text in a pull request could have a reviewer send out a token that writes to the repository. Nothing would report it.

ryan.assumes: GitHub's issue timeline gives a `commented` event the comment's author as `.user.login`, which `flag-unfinished.sh` now requires to be `github-actions[bot]`. I did not check this against GitHub; the tests use a stand-in.
ryan.if_wrong: The time-limit marker is never counted, so a build that stops at its time limit is started again each time with no stop, and each start spends Claude usage and runner minutes unnoticed.

lesson.summary: The first `ci` run after pull request #565 did what the change claimed: the two reviewers ran with no GitHub token, the `review` job posted both verdicts itself, and nothing needs changing.
lesson.detail: Pull request #565 folded the `verdicts` job into `review` in `ci.yml`: the checkout keeps no credentials, the pull request's commit is fetched with a token given to that one command, the reviewers' sessions get no `GH_TOKEN` and no `gh` tools and read what `review.sh context` wrote, and the job then posts each verdict. Run 44846307451, on pull request #568, reached 8 of the 13 changed steps and all 8 succeeded. The fetch worked with the one-command credential helper. Both carry steps found no earlier verdict, so both reviews ran. The usage-limit wait passed. The sessions' step shows only `CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN` in its environment and a tool list without `gh`. Adam and Ryan each completed (36 and 41 seconds, $0.59 and $0.61, no tool call refused or failed). The verdicts step posted both comments and saved both transcripts, and the artifact took the new name with the attempt, `session-review-44846307451-1`. The 5 skipped steps were skipped as written: the two screenshot steps because no end-to-end tests ran, and the three that ask for a person or read the time limit because nothing failed or was cancelled, so this run does not prove those paths. Adam's assumption on #565, that no file a session can read holds the job's token, is supported only in part: the checkout's cleanup found no stored credential in the repository's git config at the end of the job; other files on the runner were not checked. Ryan's assumption concerns `flag-unfinished.sh`, which this run did not use. No earlier lessons and no open tickets were given.

cost.amount: Nothing: the run succeeded, and its two reviews cost $1.20 and 77 seconds of sessions as any review does.

lesson.saves: Nothing: there was no fault to prevent.
